trainingPlans.name: Loosehead Comeback - Conditioning - Sep 2026 to Jan 2027
trainingPlans.source: Rewritten with ChatGPT, 27 September 2026; revised with Claude, 27 September 2026. Phase 1: Monday/Wednesday/Friday evening treadmill and optional short Saturday morning field practice. Phase 2: Tuesday evening floodlit field, Thursday evening treadmill maintenance, Saturday morning daylight field. Thursday field moved to Saturday because the Thursday lane is unlit. Field prescriptions, warm-ups, slow-downs, recoveries and cooldowns are in metres. Minute windows estimate scheduling only. Treadmill flow: floor mobility first, warm-up walk at start of main, uninterrupted treadmill work through walking cool-down.

goal.primaryGoal: Build a continuous 5 km aerobic base while introducing low-volume acceleration, then increase emphasis on solo rugby field conditioning alongside five weekday morning strength sessions.
goal.baseline: 4 x 5 minutes at 7 km/h, with 2 minutes walking between repetitions.

checkpoints.target: Around 30 minutes continuous at an easy pace if progression is comfortable.
First continuous 5000 m, distance led. At 7 km/h expect about 42 min 51 sec; no 30-minute requirement.
Maintain easy 5 km capacity and tolerate controlled short accelerations, shuttles and repeat efforts; review separate contact readiness.

goal.weeklySchedule: 28 September-8 November: Monday/Wednesday/Friday evenings treadmill, Saturday mornings short field technique; listed exceptions apply. First 5 km on Saturday 7 November replaces field, with Friday 6 November off. From 9 November: Tuesday evening floodlit field (Field A), Thursday evening treadmill maintenance, Saturday morning daylight field (Field B).
goal.importInstructions: Replace the previous conditioning plan using the unchanged planName. All sessions are explicitly dated in existingRunPlan; no recurring items or overrides. Keep the separate strength plan. Actual importer not tested.
goal.progressionGate: Only advance when conversational running, normal gait and next-day knee/shin response are comfortable. Repeat or shorten if needed. New swelling, locking, giving way or increasing pain means stop the provoking activity and seek assessment. Dates are provisional, not deadlines.
goal.fieldEntry: Early field work is submaximal technique, not sprint testing. Progress only with symptom-free running, comfortable leg training and good next-day recovery. After the MCL injury, seek a sports-physio return-to-sport check before faster accelerations and direction changes if readiness has not been assessed. No maximal sprinting in this plan.
goal.ifMilestoneDelayed: If 5 km is not comfortable by 7 November, retain the last successful treadmill stage on the existing Monday/Wednesday/Friday slots instead of starting the Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday block. Keep Saturday field optional or omit. Do not run both schedules. Apply the same travel/rest dates; start the first field phase when ready, never jump to a later workload.
goal.equipment: Treadmill; field timer for reference only, cones or marker bottles, measured 40 m lane plus 10 m runoff, reliable grip and lighting (Tuesday floodlights, Saturday daylight). Walk return trips to accumulate specified recovery metres.
goal.pace: Treadmill: 7 km/h starting reference, 0% incline; 6.5 km/h or slower if required for conversation. Walking recovery 4.5 km/h. Field: distance-led with perceived-speed ceilings, not stopwatch races. Acceleration walk recovery is a minimum; wait longer when needed.
goal.combinedLoad: Initial pattern is up to nine sessions across six days: five morning gym sessions, three evening treadmill sessions and one optional short field session. This is a ceiling, not a completion quota. Friday/Saturday are consecutive impact exposures, so Friday is shorter and Saturday technique is optional. Drop Saturday first if recovery is incomplete. Sunday remains rest. After 9 November, conditioning returns to three sessions weekly.
goal.buffer: All minute windows remain for importer compatibility. Field completion is determined by metres, not time; do not add repetitions to fill the booking. Time allocations include recovery, setup and transitions. Treadmill main work is time/speed led except continuous distance targets.

exceptions.reason: London travel: 5 October evening departure, 7 October away. Resume Friday 9 October.
Wedding; 31 October field is optional only if recovered.
Conditioning rest before first 5 km on Saturday 7 November.
Low Wood Bay trip; no Saturday field session. Thursday 3 December treadmill is that week's run.

goal.30Minute5K: A 30-minute 5 km requires 10 km/h. Current baseline is 4 x 5 minutes at 7 km/h. Establish continuous distance first; this block does not promise a 30-minute result. Consider a later speed-focused running block once 5 km and rugby conditioning are consistently comfortable.
goal.strengthInteraction: Monday evening treadmill follows lower-body strength: stay easy, reduce if legs are heavy. Wednesday power jumps remain optional if the added running creates soreness. Thursday treadmill after November follows morning lower-body training: keep it conversational and drop to 3 km if legs are heavy. Conditioning does not justify adding extra gym work.
goal.treadmillFlow: Floor mobility first, then one continuous treadmill visit: main begins with the five-minute warm-up walk, followed by running/recovery blocks and the walking cool-down. Final stretches follow after dismounting. All setup buffer is before boarding. Running distance targets exclude walking.

phases.focus: Time-led treadmill progression and optional short submaximal Saturday field technique.

phases.name: Continuous 5 km milestone
phases.focus: Extend easy running, then complete a distance-led 5000 m if ready.

phases.name: Rugby conditioning introduction
phases.focus: Tuesday floodlit Field A, Thursday easy treadmill maintenance, Saturday daylight Field B.

phases.name: Deload
phases.focus: Reduce field volume and treadmill distance alongside gym deload.

phases.name: Rugby conditioning build

phases.name: Consolidation
phases.focus: Lower volume, preserve quality and recover well.

readinessRules: Field distances govern completion; minute windows are only estimates. Never rush recovery to meet the timer.
Initial Saturday field is optional because it follows Friday running. Skip with heavy legs, soreness, poor sleep or adverse knee/shin response.
No maximal sprinting, sharp pivoting or contact drills. Short controlled efforts are preparation for later rugby demands.
Stop provoking work for swelling, increasing pain, locking or giving way; seek assessment.

Use a flat, well-lit, non-slippery field lane with runoff: floodlights on Tuesday, daylight on Saturday. Never run field work in the dark. If unavailable, skip field or replace with easy treadmill work, not extra sessions.
Skip field work on frost, ice or standing water; replace with easy treadmill work.
Keep the Thursday treadmill run easy after lower-body lifting. Wednesday gym jumps can be omitted when running fatigue accumulates.
Solo conditioning does not establish readiness for scrummaging, tackling or match play; arrange graded coached contact separately.
If team training begins it replaces, rather than adds to, a corresponding field session. No missed-session catch-up.

trainingPlans.name: Loosehead Comeback - Strength and Power - Sep 2026 to Jan 2027
trainingPlans.source: Written with ChatGPT, 27 September 2026; rewritten with Claude, 27 September 2026 for loosehead-prop priorities: neck-harness and neck work three times weekly, short targeted warm-ups, power movements first in most sessions, traps, adductors and scrum-posture isometrics. Four 60-minute sessions and a 45-minute Wednesday. Retained exercises keep their existing YouTube demonstrations; new exercises link to YouTube searches. Embed playback not tested.

goal.primaryGoal: Build the strength, power, neck and trunk robustness a loosehead prop needs, while rebuilding training tolerance for January 2027.
goal.scope: Monday-Friday mornings, 28 September 2026 through 4 January 2027. Four sessions capped at 60 minutes; Wednesday capped at 45. Conditioning stays in the separate plan.

weeklySplit.Thursday: Lower B - Hinge and Drive until 5 November; Upper B - Size, Traps and Neck from 12 November
weeklySplit.Friday: Upper B - Size, Traps and Neck until 6 November; Lower B - Hinge and Drive from 13 November

checkpoints.target: Complete seven introductory sessions with comfortable technique, manageable soreness and comfortable light neck-harness work.
Tolerate the main barbell lifts at two working sets and 3 RIR, and throws and swings with crisp technique; assess readiness for box jumps.
Finish deload; review gym, neck and running recovery.
Finish consolidation; assess strength, neck tolerance and separate field/contact readiness.

goal.designReason: A prop needs a strong neck, traps, trunk and posterior chain, and the power to drive. Neck work appears three times weekly (Tuesday and Upper B with the harness, Wednesday flexion and side), plus daily isometrics in the warm-up. Power comes first while fresh. Only one landing exercise per week (Monday box jump) to protect the knee alongside field work. Upper B and Lower B swap from 9 November so the Thursday evening 5 km no longer follows heavy legs.
goal.calendarSummary: 71 weekday overrides: 63 training sessions and 8 planned rest/travel dates. Seven introductory sessions. No weekend strength or catch-up sessions.

phases.name: Intro
phases.focus: Simple exercises, two easy sets; learn equipment, the hinge and very light neck-harness work. No throws or jumps.

phases.name: Base
phases.focus: Barbell lifts at two sets, 3 RIR. Throws, swings and landmine push press introduced at two sets; no jumps.

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Three sets for priority lifts and power, two for accessories. Box jumps and scrum-stance isometrics only if ready.

phases.name: Deload
phases.focus: Priority lifts and power two sets; accessories and neck one set. 4 RIR.

phases.name: Develop
phases.focus: Three sets for priority lifts, power, main accessories and harness work; about 2 RIR. Wednesday stays light.

phases.name: Consolidate
phases.focus: Two sets per exercise, 3 RIR; power two sets. No maximum tests.

strengthProgression.howToUse: All sessions are dated. The calendar selects the Intro, Base, Build, Deload, Develop or Consolidate variant with the correct sets. Read the effort target on each exercise; no manual changes required.
strengthProgression.effort: Intro 4 RIR; Base 3 RIR; Build 3 RIR; Deload 4 RIR; Develop 2 RIR; Consolidate 3 RIR. Neck work always keeps at least 3 reps in reserve. Power work has no RIR: stop each set while every rep is fast. RIR means good repetitions you could still perform.
strengthProgression.progressionRule: Reach the top of the rep range on every set with the prescribed reserve and sound technique, then add the smallest available increment next time. Typical increments: 1-2.5 kg upper-body barbell, 2.5-5 kg lower-body barbell.
strengthProgression.startingLoads: Choose loads from current ability, not old best lifts. First exposure is practice, not a test. New barbell lifts start light on 12 October. No 1RM testing.
strengthProgression.neckTraining: Start the harness at 2.5-5 kg and add only 1.25-2.5 kg once every set reaches the top of the rep range with 3 reps in reserve. Slow, controlled reps through a comfortable range; never jerk, bounce or grind. Stop for pain, pins and needles, headache or dizziness and get it checked. Daily warm-up isometrics stay at about 30% effort.
strengthProgression.powerEntry: Throws, swings and landmine push press start 12 October. Box jumps start 26 October and require comfortable lower-body training, stable controlled landings and no knee swelling, pain or instability; seek a sports-physio check if return-to-jumping readiness is uncertain. Scrum-stance isometrics start 28 October at 60-80% effort and are not contact training.
strengthProgression.powerProgression: Three sets of three at most for jumps and throws. Low box, light-moderate ball, moderate bell. Increase load or box height only when every rep is crisp; never chase exhaustion. Deload and consolidation use two sets.
strengthProgression.powerFallback: If box jumps are unsuitable, replace them with Medicine-ball scoop toss, same sets. If swings irritate the back, use Kettlebell deadlift, same sets, moving the bell fast on the way up. If the wall or ball is unsuitable, use fast incline press-ups against a fixed bar. If the knee or shoulders are symptomatic, omit the provoking movement.
strengthProgression.conditioningIntegration: Conditioning adds Monday/Wednesday/Friday evening treadmill (to 8 November), then Tuesday evening field, Thursday evening treadmill and Saturday morning field. Sunday is the full rest day. Separate morning and evening by several hours where possible. From 9 November, Thursday is an upper-body gym day so the evening 5 km follows fresh legs; Friday Lower B is followed by Saturday Field B at easy effort.
strengthProgression.wednesdayAfterField: Tuesday evening field includes accelerations. Wednesday throws and push press are optional after a demanding Tuesday; keep neck and carries easy. Never add sets to make up omitted work.
strengthProgression.fatigueRule: Finish Wednesday feeling fresh. If soreness persists into the next lower session or lifts or runs deteriorate across two sessions, drop Wednesday power first, then box jumps. If needed, use the Deload workout for the current weekday; do not force progression to meet a date.
strengthProgression.holdsAndCarries: Moderate loads, not maximum grip work. Build carries from 20 to 30 m and holds from 20 to 30 sec before adding load. Leave grip fresh for deadlifts.
strengthProgression.hardTimeLimit: Warm-up 4 min of targeted prep. Main windows include working sets, rests, ramp sets and a 1-min transition after each exercise. Cool-down starts at minute 57 (42 Wednesday). Most sessions finish with spare minutes; finish early if done.
strengthProgression.busyGym: If equipment delays eat the spare minutes, use a familiar substitute or omit the final small accessory. Never shorten necessary rest, rush technique or extend beyond the booking.
strengthProgression.warmUp: Warm-ups are four 1-minute drills, always starting with neck isometrics. Ramp sets for the first heavy lift sit in the main list directly before it, after the power exercise, so power is trained fresh.
strengthProgression.completionTiming: Every line has startMin/endMin. Tap Completed after finishing. Being ahead is fine.

gymSubstitutions.Back squat: Goblet squat, same sets and comfortable repetitions.
gymSubstitutions.Trap-bar deadlift: Romanian deadlift or Dumbbell Romanian deadlift, same sets, 6-8 reps.
gymSubstitutions.Chest-supported row: Incline-bench dumbbell row or supported row machine.
gymSubstitutions.Low step-up: Supported split squat with both feet on the floor, same sets/reps each side.
gymSubstitutions.Landmine push press: Dumbbell push press, one arm at a time, same sets.
gymSubstitutions.Scrum-stance isometric push: Omit if no padded, immovable surface is available.
gymSubstitutions.Suitcase carry: Static one-sided dumbbell hold for 20-30 seconds each side if no clear walking route.
gymSubstitutions.Neck lateral flexion (lying): Light band anchored at head height, standing side-on.
gymSubstitutions.Dumbbell shrug: Trap-bar or barbell shrug, same sets.

strengthProgression.missedSessions: Resume the next scheduled day. No doubling up and no weekend strength catch-up. Do not squeeze missed lower-body work into upper-body days.
strengthProgression.calendar: Five morning sessions per normal week. London 6-8 October, wedding 29-30 October, Low Wood Bay 7 December, Christmas Day and New Year's Day are off. Keep 5 October and 4 December mornings before travel. From 9 November Thursday is Upper B and Friday is Lower B.
strengthProgression.import: Keep the original planName to replace the previous strength plan. 30 workout definitions cover five weekdays across six phases. Each of all 71 weekdays has one strength override selecting exactly one variant or null. Actual importer not tested.
strengthProgression.videoNote: Retained exercises keep their existing YouTube demonstrations. New exercises (neck work, box jump, swings, throws, landmine push press, Copenhagen plank, shrugs, hammer curls, lateral band walk, scrum isometric) link to a YouTube search; replace with a chosen video if the app needs a single clip.

mobilityUse.summary: Warm-up mobility is built into each strength workout; no separate sessions.

recoveryUse.summary: Cool-downs are built into each strength workout; no separate sessions.

readinessRules: Assumes the MCL has healed. New swelling, giving way, locking or increasing pain: stop the provoking movement and seek assessment.
Neck work stays controlled and submaximal. Stop for pain, pins and needles, headache or dizziness and get it checked.
One landing exercise per week (Monday box jump), stepping down every rep. Jumps and throws are skipped, not forced, when readiness is uncertain.
Wednesday is a light day. Keep carries, neck and trunk work comfortably submaximal.
Scrum-stance isometrics are submaximal pushing against an immovable pad, not contact or live scrummaging.
Leave at least the prescribed reps in reserve and never force failed repetitions.
This supports a rugby return but does not establish match readiness. Live scrummaging and contact require graded, coached progression.
